english: Addendum. Some hold that realizing the ultimate basic space of phenomena, where what is cultivated and the cultivator are nondual, and becoming like two spaces mixed together, is ultimate. Here, it is not ultimate: the mere emptiness in which both object and subject are empty, without causal dependent arising becoming manifest, is like two spaces mixed together and is the clear realization of a hearer.[^N-C-047]

notes.problem: The standalone mixing family is not fully entered in the glossary, though existing compounds establish mix/mixed/mixing vocabulary.
notes.treatment: Use mixed provisionally for this explicit two-spaces analogy and keep the term linked at later doctrinal uses.
notes.uncertainty: This does not approve integrate with or a universal standalone mapping.
notes.review_action: Review the mixing construction in relation to the existing glossary compounds.

english: Vajra statement. Some say, “Of maturation and liberation, the path of liberation comprises generation and completion. Completion has two divisions: signless Mahamudra and paths of method with signs, such as the six Dharmas. The path of method is intended for the period before realization arises; once realization has arisen, it is unnecessary, like a bridge after crossing the river.”

Here, even a yogin possessing realization has particular need of the path of method. To mature and liberate beings who have not realized, miraculous powers and superknowledges are needed as a pair. Their causes—all paths of method, such as inner heat and generosity—must be practiced, because emptiness occurs as cause and result and one must act in accordance with their meaning. Accordingly, the master said:[^N-C-048]

notes.problem: ཡ་མ་ཟུང is an unusual expression here and མངོནཤེས lacks a syllable separator.
notes.treatment: Render miraculous powers and superknowledges as a pair provisionally; do not alter the source.
notes.uncertainty: The pairing expression may have another force.
notes.review_action: Check the wording and the technical term for superknowledges.

notes.problem: Three x marks interrupt the quoted verse; གཞན་དོན normally concerns others’ benefit, but its complete construction is missing.
notes.treatment: Preserve all three x marks and only translate surviving fragments, with meaning retained for དོན.
notes.uncertainty: The missing predicates and relationships are unresolved.
notes.review_action: Locate and collate the master’s quoted verse.

english: And Lord Maitreya said:

For the supreme courageous ones carrying
The great burden of beings on their heads, a leisurely pace is unbecoming.
It is as the earlier masters of this practice lineage acted.
Addendum. Others maintain the completion stage with signs, endowed with four wind practices, as follows:

First cultivate emptiness for a few days.
Then forcefully expel the wind
Three times through both nostrils.
If this is not done, it goes inside.

Then draw the wind through both nostrils
Like drawing with a hook,
Gently and at length.
By this the wind enters its own place;
If forceful, it diverts into other channel locations.
This is the wind practice of inhaling.

The wind descends through the right and left,
Like sheep intestines inflated by blowing,
Going “ha-ra-ra.”
Imagine that it enters the central channel.
This is the wind practice of filling.[^N-C-050]

notes.problem: The human reference is blank at U03820. ལུག་རྒྱུད་རྒྱུ་མ is an irregular phrase, and ha-ra-ra is an expressive sound rather than a named agent.
notes.treatment: Translate the apparent inflated-intestine simile and retain ha-ra-ra as sound.
notes.uncertainty: The sheep/intestine construction needs witness verification.
notes.review_action: Check U03820; do not infer continuum from the incidental རྒྱུད sequence.

english:
Then bring the wind into the belly
And, while able, press it down strongly.
When unable, inhale a little.
If that too is insufficient, through both nostrils
Release outward for the measure of a finger snap
And hold the remainder.
This is the wind practice of pressing.[^N-C-051]

notes.problem: The concessive ཀྱང makes the first instruction awkward; the technical name གཞིལ་བ lacks an active entry.
notes.treatment: Read while able provisionally from the following unable contrast; render the named stage as pressing.
notes.uncertainty: Precise force and conventional name require review.
notes.review_action: Check the original instructional verse and approve the local stage name.

english:
When unable to hold it and the time comes to release,
Actually release just one portion slowly
Upward through both nostrils.
As the object of focus, imagine it rising inside the central channel,
Like an arrow shot by a powerful archer,
Through Brahmā’s gate into space,
Blue and billowing as it goes.
This is the wind practice of shooting like an arrow.[^N-C-052]

notes.problem: The expressive phrase ཕྱུར་ཕྱུར and the quantity ཆ་གཅིག are not precisely specified.
notes.treatment: Retain one portion without inventing a fraction; use blue and billowing provisionally.
notes.uncertainty: The color could be conventionally called green; the motion image is uncertain.
notes.review_action: Review the image and quantity against the complete practice text.

english: Although those four are considered profound, here the profound essential point is to leave the wind uncontrived, letting it be, without holding it. Since wind-mind is not divided, even if one undertakes many compressions and agitations of the channels involving exertion and expulsion of wind and calls them yogic exercises, without seeing the natural state of ordinary mind as a thing, a few temporary, merely apparent conventional qualities may arise, but no effective accomplishment of great ultimate reach comes about.[^N-C-053]

notes.problem: The cluster describing wind effort and channel movement is irregular; the relation of སེམས and དངོས་པོ is compressed.
notes.treatment: Render the physical operations provisionally and preserve ordinary mind as the thing whose natural state is seen.
notes.uncertainty: Exact operations and syntactic attachment need confirmation.
notes.review_action: Review U03843–U03848 in a witness, without turning the rough reference into authority.

english: Therefore it is indispensable to practice the binding of the essential points of wind that generates primordial knowing realizing the inseparability of wind-mind. It is crucial to practice as taught in the Vajra Garland explanatory tantra. Understand the method through the three instructions on inner heat.[^N-C-054]

notes.problem: The phrase མ་བྱས་བྱར་མེད is interpreted as cannot do without, rather than as non-doing. This must be reconciled with the preceding uncontrived wind instruction.
notes.treatment: Translate indispensable while preserving binding; leave the three inner-heat instructions unnamed.
notes.uncertainty: The referent of three instructions and the precise idiom require review.
notes.review_action: Check the idiom and the referenced inner-heat instruction collection.

english: Addendum. Some say that transference consists of relying on HŪṂ or any other syllable and transferring into the heart of the lama or chosen deity. That applies to a gradual approach. Here, the ultimate and supreme transference is the inseparability of consciousness, the lama, and the clear-light Dharma embodiment, because there is no support for something transferred and a transferrer.
For it is said, “If there is something to transfer, it is not yoga.” Thus this is the transference of the foremost yogin.

Vajra statement. Some say that to enhance realization one must undertake various suitable activities of disciplined observance: discard the signs of ordination, wear a yogin’s dress, take a female mudrā consort along, and wander in charnel grounds, marketplaces, and so forth, singing and dancing.[^N-C-055]

notes.problem: ཕྱག་རྒྱ་མ is the female-consort noun, not a negated verb meaning without instructing a mudrā. བརྟུལ་ཞུགས lacks an active entry.
notes.treatment: Use female mudrā consort and disciplined observance provisionally, retaining the reported rather than endorsed instruction.
notes.uncertainty: The word རིགས་པ may be defective or qualify the observance.
notes.review_action: Review both technical compounds and the claim’s attribution.

english: Here, the exceptionally noble activity that is fitting and proper is precious ethical discipline. Having subdued the afflictions and differentiating conceptualization to be abandoned, the activity that enters the strength of primordial knowing is this training in denying and affirming, laid down by the Buddha’s primordial knowing of what is possible and impossible. The First Supreme also says that the supreme vajra holder is a monk. This is supreme for upholding, preserving, and spreading the teaching too, as exemplified by noble Nāgārjuna and peerless Dakpo Lhajé.

Nowadays some claim disciplined activity, adorn themselves with bone adornments, wrap themselves in dog skin, disregard cause and result, and engage in the “realized practitioner’s activity” of heedlessness about body and life. They disturb all the gods and nāgas, fill valleys with the words PHAṬ and HŪṂ, stare unblinkingly into the intervening space, and say aloud, “All phenomena are great emptiness,” while wandering pointlessly like dogs. [Ethical discipline] is far superior to their disciplined activity; hence one must proceed in the manner just described.[^N-C-056]

notes.problem: The body/life idiom is unclear; the subject of the final superior comparison is implicit. The rough reference reverses the comparison.
notes.treatment: Use heedlessness about body and life provisionally and supply [Ethical discipline] as the subject of being superior.
notes.uncertainty: The comparison is clear from context; the idiom remains uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check U03880 and retain the author’s contrast rather than endorsing the criticized activity.

english: Vajra statement. Some say, “When one realizes non-cultivation, the culmination of the four yogas, one should act in great equipoise as Bhusuku: with only perception of eating, sleeping, and walking, neither discouraged nor inflated by happiness or suffering, high or low, like a leaf carried by the wind.”

Here, unless one also possesses the three—Dharma ethical discipline, accomplishment, and immeasurable compassion—one is no different from hearers and solitary victors. First, even extremely subtle faults in one’s continuum, like a strand of hair on the palm, must be abandoned; otherwise qualities are not attained. Thus the noble master did not accomplish the yakṣa because he was attached to a clay pot, and flowers did not grow on dry wood because Dharmottara was pleased with the work on valid cognition he himself had composed.[^N-C-057]

notes.problem: The threefold list must not become four by separating Dharma from ethical discipline. ཆོས་མཆོག is read as the name Dharmottara, and the cited narratives are unverified.
notes.treatment: Keep three items and provisionally identify Dharmottara; do not assign his composition to the earlier noble master.
notes.uncertainty: The persons and stories need authentication; yakṣa accomplishment is also abbreviated.
notes.review_action: Identify both narratives and review the two agents.

english: Second, one must accomplish in one’s own continuum the immeasurable noble qualities of separation and ripening, because they do not arise without causes and conditions.

Third, having abandoned the ordinary mind that desires peace and happiness for oneself alone, one must undertake others’ ultimate benefit with immeasurable compassion; for emptiness separated from compassion becomes inferior. These three are precious.
This is the sixth section, explaining the twenty vajra statements together with five supplementary statements, summarizing the essential points of view, cultivation, and activity.

Vajra statement. According to others’ positions, at the ground of buddhahood the Dharma embodiment, knowing how things are, and the qualities of separation are ultimate; the form embodiment, knowing all that there is, and the qualities of ripening are conventional. Further, the Vajra Cutter says:

Those who see me as form,
Those who know me as an enemy,
Have entered a mistaken path;
Those people do not see me.[^N-C-058]

notes.problem: The transcript reads enemy, དགྲར, where the familiar quotation has a sound-related reading; U03914 also has compressed spelling.
notes.treatment: Translate enemy as supplied and flag it; do not silently repair the source to sound.
notes.uncertainty: This is a suspected source defect, not a verified witness variant.
notes.review_action: Collate the Vajra Cutter quotation and decide any correction in a separate edition.

english: On this basis some say that the Dharma embodiment alone is ultimate. Others say that since the basic space to be realized and the realizing conceptual mind are mixed, the Dharma embodiment too has a small conventional component. Such positions are found.[^N-C-059]

notes.problem: The standalone mixing construction remains proposed, as recorded at N-C-047.
notes.treatment: Use mixed locally for the explicit basic-space/conceptual-mind relation.
notes.uncertainty: The source phrase འདྲེས་གང་ཡོད་པས is compressed.
notes.review_action: Review the construction and retain its proposed status.

english: Here, at the resultant ground of buddhahood there is not even a phenomenon to divide through elaborating the two truths. Ultimate and conventional are posited in dependence on each other. When the result has become nondual evenness, there is no conventional dependent on an ultimate, and no ultimate dependent on that conventional. Accordingly, the Recitation of Names says:

Nondual, teaching the absence of duality,
Fully abiding at the authentic limit.
And the Vajra Garland explanatory tantra says:

Truly free from the two conceptual thoughts
Of conventional and ultimate,
Where they have authentically mixed,
That is explained as union.[^N-C-060]

notes.problem: The mixing use has no standalone approved entry; its subject is implicit.
notes.treatment: Use mixed provisionally, relating it to conventional and ultimate in the preceding lines.
notes.uncertainty: Whether the union is of the two truths or their freedom from conceptual thought needs review.
notes.review_action: Review the whole stanza; keep N-C-047’s family-level proposal status.

english: And the Root [Verses on] Discerning Knowing says:

That which arises dependently
Has no cessation and no arising,
No annihilation and no permanence,
No coming and no going,
Neither different meanings nor a single meaning.[^N-C-061]

notes.problem: དོན in this philosophical contrast can mean entities or objects, but the canonical assignment is meaning.
notes.treatment: Preserve meaning while flagging this particular usage.
notes.uncertainty: The entity sense may require a scoped exception.
notes.review_action: Review the quotation and decide a local terminology treatment.

english: And the Heart of Discerning Knowing says:
“Form is empty; emptiness is form.”
Countless such passages show that it transcends all dual phenomena.

Vajra statement. Concerning supported primordial knowing, some Prāsaṅgikas, such as Candrakīrti, say that as long as there are things to abandon, up through abandoning the subtle objects of abandonment by vajra-like deep absorption at the end of the succession, antidotal primordial knowing also exists—just as flames exist while there is wood. Accordingly:[^N-C-062]

notes.problem: Supported primordial knowing introduces an abode/support distinction continued later; རྒྱུན is not the glossary continuum.
notes.treatment: Retain supported and use succession for རྒྱུན, as in N-C-007.
notes.uncertainty: The full scholastic framework is not supplied here.
notes.review_action: Review supported primordial knowing together with the later supporting embodiment discussion.

english:
When all the dry firewood of knowables has been burned,
That peaceful [state] is the victorious ones’ Dharma embodiment.
At that time there is no arising and no cessation;
The cessation of ordinary mind is actualized through the embodiment.[^N-C-063]

notes.problem: The source reads ཞིང, field/and, where peaceful is contextually expected; the final embodiment instrument is also compressed.
notes.treatment: Mark peaceful [state] as a provisional contextual reading, retaining the original Tibetan without emendation.
notes.uncertainty: A textual defect is suspected but unverified.
notes.review_action: Collate the verse, especially ཞིང and the final agent/instrument relation.

english: And the Heart of Discerning Knowing says, “There is no primordial knowing.” Statements that it exists, they say, are made in dependence on others.[^N-C-064]

notes.problem: The expression can denote dependence on others here, rather than the technical other-powered nature proposed by the rough reference.
notes.treatment: Use made in dependence on others provisionally, with statements as subject.
notes.uncertainty: Its precise hermeneutic force is not explicit.
notes.review_action: Review this use with the Prāsaṅgika attribution.

english: Svātantrikas such as Bhāvaviveka, by contrast, say that [describing] ultimate primordial knowing is like measuring space in fathoms or drawing a picture on it with colors. Merely hearing of that primordial knowing and entertaining doubt about it renders saṃsāra powerless. The Four Hundred says:[^N-C-065]

notes.problem: The source has མཚོན, which can suggest weapons rather than pigments; the two analogies share space as their apparent object. The action describing is implicit.
notes.treatment: Supply [describing] and provisionally interpret མཚོན as colors, not a weapon.
notes.uncertainty: Both the exact source form and omitted verbal relationship need checking.
notes.review_action: Collate the analogy and confirm the syntax.

english:
Whoever hears this Dharma,
Or even entertains doubt after hearing it,
Makes existence fall to tatters.
So it is said.
